title: UK monthly GDP + Index of Production + Index of Services, August 2026 (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET) — one slot, three bulletins
source: EST: three ONS release pages, first fetched direct by the proposing lane 2026-09-10 and re-fetched direct by this lane's own initial research 2026-09-30 (all HTTP 200, unchanged) — ons.gov.uk/releases/gdpmonthlyestimateukaugust2026, .../indexofproductionukaugust2026 and .../indexofservicesukaugust2026 — all three still reading verbatim 'Release date: 15 October 2026 7:00am' and 'This release is not yet published'. NOTE THE DISTINCTION THE PUBLISHER MAKES: these carry a plain 'Release date', not the 'Provisional release date' that the Blue Book 2026 and Pink Book 2026 compendium pages carry — the ONS treats the monthly slot as firm and the October compendium slot as provisional. The prior edition in the same series (July 2026 data) published 2026-09-11 on schedule, and the next edition (September 2026 data) reads '12 November 2026 7:00am' on all three latest-bulletin pages, a four-week cadence consistent with the monthly series. Filed estimate on two counts only, one fewer than the compendium entries: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a foreign national statistics institute, and this lane does not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep or inherited from a proposal — the date itself is not labelled provisional by anyone
notes: PROPOSED BY THE uk-blue-book-2026-10-30 LANE, 2026-09-10, during that event's never-assessed initial research, as the load-bearing date under that lane's central finding (every Blue Book input is public 15 days before the compendium). Read in full before this file was written. Independently, this is the UK's own most timely activity read and closes a real coverage gap: this calendar tracked UK CPI, PPI, labour market, public sector finances and quarterly national accounts, but no UK monthly output series at all. This lane's own initial research (docs/research/events/uk-monthly-gdp-2026-10-15.md) re-verified the date on two independent fetches 20 days apart, added the most recent published trend (July 2026: GDP +0.4% m/m and +0.4% 3m/3m, services +0.6% 3m/3m the strongest contributor, production and construction both -0.5% 3m/3m), and confirmed no market impact study exists or was run — no house playbook is UK-, rates- or sterling-keyed, symbols is empty, and the LOW tier is inherited from the ONS macro-print family, matching this calendar's treatment of uk-cpi-2026-09-16 and uk-quarterly-national-accounts-2026-09-30. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this.
